concept.name: Dividend risk
concept.definition: Dividend risk is the risk to a short call writer that the call is exercised early, just before the underlying's ex-dividend date, because the holder wants to own the stock in time to receive the dividend. It also refers more broadly to the effect of expected dividends on option prices — calls are cheaper and puts richer the larger the anticipated dividend.
concept.intuition: Options do not pay dividends, so the day before a payout, an in-the-money call holder may grab the stock (and its dividend) by exercising — leaving you, the writer, assigned and delivering shares plus the dividend's value.
concept.mechanics: A call holder is entitled to the dividend only if they exercise before the ex-dividend date; per OCC/OIC guidance, early exercise is rational when the dividend exceeds the call's remaining time value, so assignment probability on short ITM calls rises into ex-dates. Assigned writers must deliver stock and may be notified only after the ex-date, making the exposure invisible until it has happened.
concept.formula: Early-exercise trigger (rule of thumb): dividend > call time value remaining; with multiple dividends remaining, compare against time value of the earliest profitable exercise.
concept.failure_modes: Covered-call and spread writers who ignore dividend calendars are assigned at the worst moment, losing stock before the dividend and breaking hedges; deep ITM short call legs of spreads are prime targets, and the residual long leg plus new short stock changes the account's risk profile overnight.
concept.misconceptions: Dividends are not 'extra return' for option holders — option strike prices are not adjusted for ordinary dividends, so the stock's ex-date drop mechanically transfers value from calls to puts, and only exercise before the ex-date captures the payment.
concept.example: XYZ pays $1.00 tomorrow (ex-date); the $45 call with stock at $50 trades at $5.05 ($0.05 time value). Since $1.00 > $0.05, holders exercise en masse, and writers of that call should expect assignment tonight.
